clue.text: Go and get married again

definitions.meaning: to go somewhere is to ... there, an old-fashioned sense of betaking oneself
split as ..., to pair off once more

explanation.surface: Someone heads off to marry for a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Repair as a verb of motion is a formal synonym for going, as in repairing to the drawing room.

clue.text: Wanting for example to replace head of state? An obsessive conceit

indicators.note: one piece takes the place of the first letter of another

parts.note: Romania is a European state

explanation.surface: A would-be leader eager to replace the head of state is consumed by vanity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to replace head of' swaps the R that begins ROMANIA for EG. 'Wanting' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: Egomania is an obsessive preoccupation with oneself, an extreme form of conceit or vanity.

clue.text: Same element turned up in some protein

indicators.note: the reversed pieces go inside the word for some

parts.note: any means some, as in have you any

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means read from the bottom upward

parts.note: DO is short for ditto, meaning the same
a bit is an element or small part

explanation.surface: A chemistry note about the same element found reversed within a protein.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses DO + BIT to TIBOD, which goes 'in' ANY. 'element' suggests chemistry but means a small part.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibodies are blood proteins made by the immune system to neutralise foreign substances.

clue.text: Fabric with border imported to make carpet

indicators.note: brought in, so one piece is put inside another

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric used for upholstery
and means with, joining things
a rim is a border or edge

explanation.surface: A rug made from imported fabric with an edging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carpet' is the verb, to scold, not a rug.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is British slang for calling them in to reprimand them.

clue.text: Hollywood's easy task making funny film

definitions.meaning: American slang for something done with no effort at all
the 1933 Marx Brothers comedy of that title

explanation.surface: Making a comedy is a breeze for Hollywood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollywood's' marks the first sense as American slang; the film is the Marx Brothers' 1933 comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is US slang for a trivially easy job and also the title of a classic comedy film.

clue.text: Contented with entire arrangement? Refugee might be held here

indicators.note: an arrangement puts the letters of both words into a new order

explanation.surface: A question of whether a contented refugee would accept an entire rearrangement of their life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' shuffles CONTENTED and ENTIRE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Asylum seekers are often confined in such a facility while their claims are processed.

clue.text: Pub entertainment said to give US statesman a lift

indicators.note: said means the letters come from what is heard, not what is written

parts.note: to carry an Okie, a man from the US state of Oklahoma, so a state's man

explanation.surface: A pub singalong is reported to give an American politician a boost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'statesman' is punningly a state's man: an Okie, from Oklahoma. Carry Okie sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Karaoke, singing along to backing tracks, is a popular evening entertainment in pubs and bars.

clue.text: Tiny size of fleet is a joke

definitions.meaning: a fleet of only one ocean liner
a short quip delivered in a single sentence

explanation.surface: A navy with very few ships is a laughing stock.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense splits as ONE LINER: a single ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-liner is a brief joke, and a fleet consisting of one liner is a tiny one.

clue.text: Study in order to improve modern language at university

parts.note: Polish is the language of Poland
up means in residence at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student goes up to university to work on a modern language.
explanation.walkthrough: UP for at university is a British idiom: one goes up to Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: To polish up a skill is to work at it and refine it, studying to get better.

clue.text: Fondness of drunks, one for gulping loudly, one for sipping quietly?

indicators.note: a drunk gulping something takes it inside, so a letter goes into the first sot

parts.note: a sot is a drunkard; the plural supplies two of them
F is forte, the musical direction for loud

indicators.note: the second drunk sipping takes a letter in, so it goes inside the other sot

parts.note: the second of the two drunkards, another sot
P is piano, the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Two drinkers, one swigging noisily and one sipping softly, share an affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunks' gives two sots: 'one for gulping loudly' puts F inside one, and 'one for sipping quietly' puts P inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a soft spot for someone is the idiom for a particular fondness or affection.

clue.text: Men with skill who wrote novels?

parts.note: OR is other ranks, the ordinary soldiers as opposed to officers
doing something well is doing it with skill

explanation.surface: A question about which skilful men were novelists.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, is the army's term for enlisted men.
explanation.definitionFit: George Orwell is the novelist behind Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four, so he is one who wrote novels.

clue.text: Taking a third from university, with a note in Welsh

indicators.note: removing a third of a word's letters means the last three of its nine go

parts.note: Cambridge is the English university town
N is a standard abbreviation for note, as in footnotes

explanation.surface: A student graduates with a third-class degree and a remark written in Welsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking a third from' drops DGE, the last three of CAMBRIDGE's nine letters, leaving CAMBRI. The surface suggests a third-class degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambria is the Latin name for Wales, so Cambrian is a literary adjective meaning Welsh.

clue.text: Name of Smollett's book addressing prejudice?

definitions.meaning: a book of the Apocrypha, also called Tobit
speaking to prejudice, with the question mark flagging the punning split

explanation.surface: A question about the title of a Smollett novel concerning bigotry.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface invents a Smollett novel; in fact three readings meet: the novelist's first name, a book of the Apocrypha, and TO BIAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Tobias Smollett wrote Roderick Random, and Tobias is the name of an apocryphal book of the Bible.

clue.text: Expression of anxiety? Mere idea is absurd

indicators.note: absurd means nonsensical, so the letters of the phrase are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a mere idea as ridiculous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is absurd' rearranges MERE IDEA.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old-fashioned exclamation of dismay or worry, the sort a fretful person mutters.

clue.text: Like a girl, bowled over by his manoeuvring?

parts.note: a maiden is an over bowled in cricket with no runs scored

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves things around, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A girl is swept off her feet by a man's scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled over' looks like smitten, but a maiden over is a cricket term: six balls bowled with no runs. 'manoeuvring' rearranges HIS to ISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Maidenish describes behaviour typical of a maiden, a young unmarried girl.

clue.text: One minute perhaps before sailor boarded?

indicators.note: a sailor who boarded has gone inside, so the seaman's letters go into the other word

parts.note: by means before, as in finishing by noon
AB is an able-bodied seaman

explanation.surface: Someone arrived a minute before the sailor got aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' is the adjective for tiny, not sixty seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby is an example of a minute, tiny one, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Approximate location of pitcher?

definitions.meaning: in a ... figure, meaning rough or estimated
a baseball stadium, where the pitcher throws

explanation.surface: A question about roughly where a jug might be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitcher' suggests a jug, but it is the baseball player.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballpark figure is a rough estimate, and a ballpark is a baseball ground where the pitcher plays.

clue.text: Fashionable phrase used in phone call, given news

parts.note: to give someone a buzz is to phone them
word means news, as in any word from home

explanation.surface: A trendy expression slips into a telephone conversation with fresh news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given' is a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzword is a trendy piece of jargon that becomes fashionable for a while.

clue.text: Pendant found in shed

definitions.meaning: to let fall or lose, as a tree does its leaves

explanation.surface: A piece of jewellery turns up in a garden shed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shed' looks like the garden hut; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop is a pendant earring, and to drop leaves is to shed them.

clue.text: Typo said possibly to be in worst imaginable place

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters may form something else when reordered

explanation.surface: A misprint is claimed to make somewhere the worst place imaginable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges TYPO and SAID together.
explanation.definitionFit: A dystopia is an imagined society of the worst kind, the opposite of a utopia.

clue.text: Lost without one fellow, needless to say

indicators.note: without one means minus a single letter

parts.note: off course means having strayed from the route, lost
F is fellow; only one of the two Fs goes

explanation.surface: Someone lost a companion, which goes without saying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one fellow' removes just one of the two Fs in OFF COURSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Of course is an everyday phrase meaning naturally, it goes without saying.

clue.text: State body that singles you out

parts.note: ID is the postal abbreviation for Idaho, a US state
an entity is a body or being that exists in its own right

explanation.surface: A government agency picks out individual citizens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State body' reads as a public authority, but it splits into Idaho's abbreviation and a synonym for body.
explanation.definitionFit: Your identity is what makes you distinct from everyone else, marking you out as an individual.

clue.text: Same girl Jack dumped twice introduced with no love lost

indicators.note: one letter is brought in between the two copies
the same piece is used two times over
Jack dumped means the J is dropped from the girl

parts.note: Jill is a girl's name, the Jill of Jack and Jill
J is the abbreviation for jack in cards

explanation.surface: Jill, twice dumped by Jack, ends up with no love lost between them.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme pairing is misdirection: 'dumped' drops J from JILL, 'twice' doubles the result, and 'introduced' puts W between.
explanation.definitionFit: No love lost is the idiom for mutual dislike or hostility between two people.

clue.text: First and last characters to get into lotus position in shiftless way

indicators.note: one piece getting into another goes inside it

parts.note: the lotus is a water lily, and the flower's position is taken as the flower itself
A and Z are the first and last letters of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A yoga instruction about letters settling into the lotus position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lotus position' suggests yoga; the lotus is a water lily. 'First and last characters' are A and Z, put inside after the L.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something lazily is acting idly, in an indolent, shiftless manner.

clue.text: Kicking out after blues missed header

indicators.note: the word lacks its header, its first letter

parts.note: dejection is low spirits, a fit of the blues

explanation.surface: A footballer misses a header and gets a kicking from the fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed header' takes D off DEJECTION; the football picture is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: An ejection is a throwing or kicking out, as of a troublemaker from a ground.

clue.text: Bother! Sent back wrong dish

parts.note: ado is fuss or bother

indicators.note: read backwards, as a meal sent back to the kitchen

parts.note: a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A diner complains and sends back the wrong dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dish' is slang for a good-looking person, not a plate of food; the surface's restaurant complaint is misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Adonis was the beautiful youth of Greek myth, so his name stands for any handsome man, slang dish.

clue.text: Tourists switch operators

definitions.meaning: devices that trip a switch, things that throw it

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers change tour operators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'switch' looks like a verb, swapping tour firms; it is the electrical switch.
explanation.definitionFit: Trippers are people on short pleasure trips, and a tripper is also a mechanism that trips a switch.

clue.text: Extremely tactful young person meeting sweetheart after midnight

indicators.note: the sweetheart's letters come after those from midnight

parts.note: a kid is a child
the middle letter of the word night
love is a term of endearment for a sweetheart

explanation.surface: A youngster meets a lover after midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' gives G, the middle of NIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Kid-glove handling is very gentle and tactful, after soft gloves of kid leather.

clue.text: Woman ditching second husband, forty-five?

indicators.note: to ditch the second of something is to drop the later one, so the second matching letter is removed

parts.note: Heather is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman of forty-five gets rid of her second husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forty-five' looks like her age; it is a .45 pistol, and heater is slang for a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Heater is underworld slang for a handgun, and a forty-five is a .45-calibre pistol.
